## How we work with you

- You keep your own Login.gov account. We never sign in as you.

- You answer every certification yourself. We explain each one first.

- Our prices, and when you get a refund, are on the pricing page. See pricing

## What your AI employee does

### Your registration

- Asks you SAM.gov's questions one at a time, and says what each one is for.

- Checks the format of each answer.

- On a renewal, notes where an answer differs from your public record.

- Reads the documents you upload and proposes answers. You confirm each one.

- Puts your answers into a worksheet, in SAM.gov's order.

Everything here but reading a filing or certificate you upload runs on fixed rules and contains no AI-generated text. From a state filing or a certificate of good standing, the AI assistant may read the business's name and address; an ID or a contact card is read by Firmenza's own code.

Open the copilot

### Watching your registration

- Every day, re-reads the public SAM.gov record of the registrations you watch, the closest to their expiration date first and as many as SAM.gov's daily limit allows.

- Emails you reminders from 75 days before the expiration date, with the real date.

- Near the expiration date, shows what to have ready for your renewal, beside what your public record said.

- Tells you when a read finds a change: the status, the expiration date, or details such as the legal name, the address or the CAGE code.

- After a renewal, your watch list shows the new expiration date once the public record does.

- Up to three more people can get a registration's reminders, each once they confirm by email.

- “What buyers see on your public record” lists what the record showed on our last read.

The watch runs on fixed rules and contains no AI-generated text.

Your watch list and reminders Run a free health check

### Finding contract opportunities and grants

- Daily matches with SAM.gov's contract opportunities, by NAICS code, state and keyword, each saying why it matched.

- Keywords to leave out keep the notices you don't want out of your matches.

- Saved notices keep a private note and tell you what changed, such as a moved response date.

- A digest email of new matches and changes, once a day or once a week.

- “Explain this notice”, a plain summary from the AI assistant, drawn from the notice's published fields and marking what it does not state.

- “Before you respond”, a short checklist on each notice still open to a response, including whether your registration is active through its response date and whether your public record lists its NAICS code.

- On a notice's page, the link the agency added to it, when GSA's file has one.

- A requirements checklist on a notice you save: upload its solicitation, and Firmenza's rules list what it asks for, with the page of each. You track each one, and print the list or download it.

- The market view: who buys what you sell, from past contract awards in your codes.

- Also in the market view: contracts in your codes that end within the next year.

- Grant matches from Grants.gov, with keywords of their own, once you turn them on.

- New York City bid notices, matched by keyword, once you turn them on.

Everything in this list comes with Pro's contract and grant matches, digest and market view, with a 14-day trial.

Everything here but “Explain this notice” runs on fixed rules and contains no AI-generated text. These are tools to help you find and pursue contracts, and the decision to bid is always yours.

Contract opportunities in Firmenza

### Ask Firmenza

- On Firmenza's pages, the AI assistant answers questions about Firmenza, SAM.gov and your registration, in English or Spanish.

- It answers from Firmenza's own guides, with links to read more.

- Signed in, it can also tell you the public status and expiration date of the registrations you watch.

- It never says how to answer a certification. On size, affiliation, ownership, exclusions or lobbying, it explains the words and refers you to a free counselor or an attorney.

- In the copilot, it answers about the section you are on, and can follow on from your last two questions there.

- Signed in, you can choose how it words its answers to you, such as shorter answers or numbered steps.

Wherever it talks, its words carry the “AI assistant” label.

SAM.gov and Login.gov are for people, so the AI assistant never signs in, never enters anything in SAM.gov and never makes a certification. A Firmenza specialist reviews your application. You make every certification yourself. We explain each one first.
